key_nl_quotes: The NSM state machine has three hierarchical layers (i.e., composite behaviours) that are implemented with the region, state and substate scalar variables.

The alarm transition is triggered either when: the operator presses the alarm interrupter on the HMI; the liquid volume within the mixing tank is above a high threshold limit value; the acid or the concentrated nutrient tanks must be refilled.
one_line_pitch: This is a hard industrial HSM stress test because hierarchy, parent-level actions, entry/exit behavior, threshold guards, and alarm-stop logic are distributed across the process description and PLC implementation.
rationale: The sample directly targets Apvrille-style weak points: hierarchical states are explicit, actions include entry/exit and parent-level actuator behavior, and guards combine several process and operator conditions. It also has a dedicated alarm stop path grounded in real sensor conditions. The information is split across physical-process prose, state-machine discussion, and PLC implementation details, making it a strong benchmark case rather than a thin toy FSM.
